evals.name: console-connect-and-append
evals.prompt: Write a C# console app (not Arc) that connects to a local Chronicle development server, gets an event store called 'quickstart', and appends a `FundsDeposited(decimal Amount)` event for account 'account-1', handling the failure case. Give the code in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: ChronicleClient built with ChronicleConnectionString.Development, GetEventStore, an [EventType] record with no id argument, eventStore.EventLog.Append returning AppendResult checked via IsSuccess, with no IChronicleClient.Connect.
assertions: Constructs ChronicleClient with ChronicleConnectionString.Development and calls GetEventStore rather than a nonexistent IChronicleClient.Connect.
Declares the event as a record marked [EventType] without passing an id, since the type name is the identifier.
Appends through eventStore.EventLog.Append with the event source id first and the event second.
Checks the AppendResult (IsSuccess, ConstraintViolations, ConcurrencyViolation or Errors) instead of assuming success.

evals.name: standalone-defaults
evals.prompt: A standalone .NET worker using the Cratis.Chronicle client has a reactor whose constructor takes an `IEmailSender`. The reactor throws NullReference-style failures, there are no client logs, and the app exits right after appending so the reactor never runs. Explain each cause and the fixes. Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Default IServiceProvider activates via Activator.CreateInstance so pass a real container; default ILoggerFactory is silent so supply one; observation is a live gRPC stream so keep the process alive.
assertions: Explains that the default IServiceProvider constructs observers with Activator.CreateInstance so a reactor with constructor dependencies is default-constructed unless a real container is passed.
Says the default ILoggerFactory is a silent one, so supply an ILoggerFactory to see client diagnostics.
Says observation is a live duplex stream, so a console app that appends and returns from Main never sees a reactor run; keep the process alive.

evals.name: readiness-and-tls
evals.prompt: A team polls `IsConnected` before starting work, ships the default TLS behavior to production, and copied the package version from the repo's csproj. What is wrong with each? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Connected is not registered, so use WaitForRegistration; certificate validation is skipped by default so production sets skipTlsValidation=false; the repo version is a placeholder, take it from nuget.org.
assertions: States that connected is not the same as registered and recommends WaitForRegistration instead of polling IsConnected.
States that certificate validation is skipped by default and a production connection string must set skipTlsValidation=false.
States that the version in the repository is a placeholder and the version should be taken from nuget.org.

evals.name: host-registration
evals.prompt: A developer writes `services.AddCratisChronicle(...)` on an IServiceCollection and `builder.WithClaimsBasedNamespaceResolver()`; neither compiles. What are the real APIs for a worker or ASP.NET host and for a plain IServiceCollection? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: AddCratisChronicle is an extension on IHostApplicationBuilder/WebApplicationBuilder; IServiceCollection has AddCratisChronicleClient and AddCratisChronicleConnection; WithClaimsBasedNamespaceResolver does not exist.
assertions: States AddCratisChronicle is an extension on IHostApplicationBuilder (and WebApplicationBuilder), not IServiceCollection.
Names AddCratisChronicleClient and AddCratisChronicleConnection as the IServiceCollection extensions.
States that WithClaimsBasedNamespaceResolver is not a real extension.
